findings.highlight: Rin has cut down the endless barrage of dark curses.
findings.evidenceJa: 黒身の呪いを、凛は一刀の下に両断していた。
findings.governingReading: Rin has bisected the black-bodied curses under single strokes of her blade.
findings.explanation: The English removes bisection, the one-stroke method, and the giant bodies, replacing them with a barrage.

findings.highlight: Each of the black giants is a match for the Noble Phantasms wielded by Servants.
findings.evidenceJa: 一体一体がサーヴァントの持つ宝具に匹敵する。
findings.governingReading: Each black giant matches a Noble Phantasm possessed by a Servant.
findings.explanation: The plural English comparison can make each giant equal multiple Noble Phantasms rather than one.

findings.highlight: running up the cliff now
findings.evidenceJa: 苦もなく崖を駆け上がりながら
findings.governingReading: Rin runs up the cliff without difficulty while erasing the shadows.
findings.explanation: The English removes the ease that shocks Sakura and establishes Rin’s apparent dominance.

findings.highlight: emits seven prismatic colors
findings.evidenceJa: 七色に輝き
findings.governingReading: The formerly colorless blade shines in seven colors.
findings.explanation: The English awkwardly makes the blade emit colors as objects rather than shine chromatically.

findings.highlight: extraordinary power surging from its core.
findings.evidenceJa: 桁外れの魔力を提供し
findings.governingReading: The sword’s center supplies an extraordinary quantity of magical energy.
findings.explanation: The English changes provision of the technical resource into a generic power surge.

findings.highlight: Destroying the last of the shadows in her way
findings.evidenceJa: 侵入を拒んでいた影たちを一掃し
findings.governingReading: Rin sweeps away the shadows that had refused her entry.
findings.explanation: The English invents that these are the last shadows and removes their gatekeeping function.

findings.highlight: The black girl stares with surprise
findings.evidenceJa: 黒い少女は愕然と
findings.governingReading: Blackened Sakura stares in stunned astonishment.
findings.explanation: Surprise weakens her shocked loss of composure.

findings.highlight: “No wayit’s not possible.”
findings.evidenceJa: 「うそそんな、はず」
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s disbelief breaks into incomplete fragments: “No… that can’t…”
findings.explanation: The English supplies a complete proposition while visibly fusing way and it’s.

findings.highlight: the things behind her
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女の背後に浮かぶモノ
findings.governingReading: The unidentified thing floating behind Sakura may sense its master’s crisis.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes the guarded singular presence.

findings.highlight: You’re not holding back.
findings.evidenceJa: また大盤振舞ね。
findings.governingReading: Rin jokes that Sakura is making another lavish, generous expenditure.
findings.explanation: The English states effort level and removes Rin’s resource-spending joke.

findings.highlight: strength to even kill one of my shadows
findings.evidenceJa: 影を消す魔力
findings.governingReading: Rin lacks the magical energy needed to erase even one shadow.
findings.explanation: The English changes magical energy into strength and erasure into killing.

findings.highlight: The light of Saber’s Noble Phantasm, Excalibur.
findings.evidenceJa: エクスカリバーの光そのものではないか、と少女は歯を軋ませる。
findings.governingReading: Sakura grinds her teeth at the thought that the flashes may be Excalibur’s own light.
findings.explanation: The English leaves a noun fragment, removes uncertainty, and omits Sakura grinding her teeth.

findings.highlight: a poor imitation of the Third Sorcery
findings.evidenceJa: 第三魔法の出来そこない
findings.governingReading: Sakura is a defective or failed realization of the Third Magic.
findings.explanation: Imitation suggests deliberate copying and blurs Magic into sorcery.

findings.highlight: I use an imitation of my great master, who travels across infinite parallel worlds.
findings.evidenceJa: 無限に列なる並行世界を旅する爺さんの模造品
findings.governingReading: Rin calls herself an imitation of the old man who travels infinitely arrayed parallel worlds.
findings.explanation: The English makes Rin use an imitation of her teacher rather than identify herself as the imitation.

findings.highlight: a copycat of the Second Sorcery
findings.evidenceJa: 第二魔法の泥棒猫
findings.governingReading: Rin jokingly calls herself a thieving cat of the Second Magic.
findings.explanation: Copycat replaces theft with imitation and blurs Magic into sorcery.

findings.highlight: Light and heat, like those of a miniature Excalibur, send rumbles through the cavern.
findings.evidenceJa: 光と熱は内壁を削り
findings.governingReading: The miniature-Excalibur light and heat shave away the inner wall and shake the cavern.
findings.explanation: The English omits physical erosion of the cavern wall.

findings.highlight: you’re hiding yourself in the shadows.
findings.evidenceJa: 影に守られて出てこない
findings.governingReading: Sakura is protected by shadows and will not come out.
findings.explanation: The English changes being guarded and refusing to emerge into active hiding inside the shadows.

findings.highlight: she summons the shadows out of fear.
findings.evidenceJa: 怖れだけで影たちを使役する。
findings.governingReading: Sakura commands the existing shadows from fear alone.
findings.explanation: The English changes control of the shadows into bringing them into existence.

findings.highlight: it cannot be used within a lifetime
findings.evidenceJa: 時代の一生を以ってしても使い切れぬ量
findings.governingReading: The reserve could not be exhausted even across the lifetime of an era.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the scale to one person’s lifetime.

findings.highlight: a thousand magical energy
findings.evidenceJa: 一千程度の魔力
findings.governingReading: Rin needs roughly one thousand units of magical energy each time.
findings.explanation: The English uses an uncountable noun with a bare numeral and omits the approximate unit sense.

findings.highlight: Such a large supply of magical energy
findings.evidenceJa: バカみたいに肥大した魔力
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s absurdly bloated magical reserve is treasure left to rot unused.
findings.explanation: The English removes Rin’s contemptuous bloated-body image.

findings.highlight: If a thousand light is smashed against a thousand shadow, the powers will certainly cancel each other.
findings.evidenceJa: 千の魔力に対する千の光ならば、確かに力は拮抗する。
findings.governingReading: One thousand units of light opposed to one thousand units of magical energy can genuinely contend on equal terms.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes shadow for mana and cancellation for equilibrium.

findings.highlight: creates the competition that should not be possible.
findings.evidenceJa: 成立しない拮抗を生み出す
findings.governingReading: The sword creates an equilibrium that ordinarily could not exist.
findings.explanation: Competition is malformed and loses the precise equality of forces.

findings.highlight: It’s not using Tohsaka Rin’s magical energy.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂凛の魔力を増幅しての事ではない。
findings.governingReading: The output does not result from amplifying Rin’s own magical energy.
findings.explanation: The English falsely says her mana is not used at all, confusing use with amplification.

findings.highlight: eliminate a giant.
findings.evidenceJa: 影の巨人を退けられる
findings.governingReading: Atmospheric mana could let Rin repel a shadow giant once.
findings.explanation: The English strengthens temporary repulsion into elimination.

findings.highlight: Air holds a finite amount of power.
findings.evidenceJa: 大気の魔力とて有限
findings.governingReading: Even magical energy in the atmosphere is finite.
findings.explanation: The English replaces a technical resource with generic power held by air.

findings.highlight: in this world.
findings.evidenceJa: この大空洞で
findings.governingReading: Within this great cavern, Rin can oppose Sakura only once.
findings.explanation: The English expands the local mana condition to the entire world.

findings.highlight: a parallel world
findings.evidenceJa: 合わせ鏡のように列なる『ここと同じ場所』
findings.governingReading: Identical places line up across parallel worlds like facing mirrors.
findings.explanation: The English removes the mirror-array structure and the same-location condition.

findings.highlight: taking a thousand magical energy from one of the infinite parallel worlds
findings.evidenceJa: 毎回一千ずつ魔力を集めて
findings.governingReading: Rin gathers one thousand units each time from the infinite facing-mirror worlds.
findings.explanation: The English makes the source one world and omits the repeated per-strike cycle.

findings.highlight: The girl drawing a massive supply from the Great Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 大聖杯という、巨大な貯蔵庫を持つ少女
findings.governingReading: The girl possesses the enormous reservoir called the Greater Grail.
findings.explanation: The English changes possession of the reservoir into the ongoing act of drawing from it.

findings.highlight: makes a path in between infinite parallel worlds.
findings.evidenceJa: 並行世界に路を繋げる
findings.governingReading: Zelretch connects a path to the infinitely arrayed parallel worlds.
findings.explanation: In between obscures the directed connection from this world to an adjacent possibility.

findings.highlight: another possible world.
findings.evidenceJa: 隣り合う『違う可能性を持つ』世界
findings.governingReading: The implement peers into an adjacent world possessing a different possibility.
findings.explanation: The English removes adjacency and weakens a world with another possibility into an indefinite possible world.

findings.highlight: nor does it have the power to create energy when swung.
findings.evidenceJa: 一撃振るう度に千の魔力を生み出す力もない。
findings.governingReading: The sword cannot itself create one thousand units of mana with every strike.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the quantity and repeated per-strike scope.

findings.highlight: She can move on to the next one
findings.evidenceJa: 使いきれば次に移ればいい。
findings.governingReading: Once one cavern’s mana is exhausted, Rin moves to the next parallel world’s corresponding cavern.
findings.explanation: The English leaves the object as an undefined one and can suggest Rin herself travels.

findings.highlight: The possibility of opposite mirrors
findings.evidenceJa: 合わせ鏡の可能性
findings.governingReading: The possibilities repeat like facing mirrors.
findings.explanation: Opposite mirrors is nonidiomatic and does not express mutually facing recursive reflections.

findings.highlight: the two magi are equal!
findings.evidenceJa: 二つの事柄はまったくの同位である！
findings.governingReading: With equal Magic-Circuit performance, inexhaustible storage and indefinitely repeated supply are operationally equivalent.
findings.explanation: The English falsely declares Rin and Sakura themselves equal rather than the two mana-supply conditions.

findings.highlight: the altar and the Great Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 大聖杯たるこの祭壇
findings.governingReading: This altar, which is the Greater Grail, will not survive the collapse.
findings.explanation: The English splits one appositional identity into two coordinated objects.

findings.highlight: if she continues fighting.
findings.evidenceJa: このまま徒に戦いを続けては
findings.governingReading: If Sakura continues the battle pointlessly, she will lose.
findings.explanation: The English removes the judgment that continuing this exchange is futile.

findings.highlight: the room will cave in
findings.evidenceJa: 洞窟の崩壊
findings.governingReading: The cave itself will collapse after Rin’s stamina gives out.
findings.explanation: Room reduces the scale and changes the named environment.

findings.highlight: understand the origin of her enemy’s power.
findings.evidenceJa: 敵の正体が判った
findings.governingReading: Sakura finally understands the true identity or nature of her enemy.
findings.explanation: The English narrows identity to the source of Rin’s power.

findings.highlight: Gasping for breath, Sakura glares at her older sister.
findings.evidenceJa: 大きく肩を揺らし、苦しげに吐息をもらして、間桐桜は悠然と佇む姉を睨む。
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s shoulders heave and painful breaths escape as she glares at her sister standing composed and unhurried.
findings.explanation: The English removes Sakura’s shoulder movement and Rin’s contrasting calm posture.

findings.highlight: Have you cooled your head now?
findings.evidenceJa: 舞い上がってた頭も、これで少しは冷えたでしょ
findings.governingReading: Rin asks whether Sakura’s carried-away, overheated head has cooled a little.
findings.explanation: The English preserves cooling but drops the prior excited or conceited state and degree.

findings.highlight: that she’s pushing herself into a corner.
findings.evidenceJa: 自らの首を絞めると理解していながら
findings.governingReading: Sakura continues despite knowing she is strangling herself through the battle.
findings.explanation: The English replaces lethal self-destruction with tactical disadvantage.

findings.highlight: The grudge she kept inside
findings.evidenceJa: 唯一の肉親に対する恨み
findings.governingReading: The accumulated grudge is directed at her only blood relative.
findings.explanation: The English removes Rin as the uniquely intimate object of Sakura’s resentment.

findings.highlight: That’s why I want to win.
findings.evidenceJa: だから勝ちたかった。
findings.governingReading: Sakura explains why she had wanted to win and receive praise.
findings.explanation: The English shifts the confession into a current competitive desire.

findings.highlight: the room with worms
findings.evidenceJa: 暗い蟲倉
findings.governingReading: Sakura was confined in the dark worm storehouse.
findings.explanation: The English removes both darkness and the established torture-space designation.

findings.highlight: was treated as an object
findings.evidenceJa: 毎日毎日オモチャみたいに扱われてた
findings.governingReading: Every day Sakura was treated like a toy.
findings.explanation: The English removes relentless repetition and the dehumanizing plaything comparison.

findings.highlight: the miserable girl
findings.evidenceJa: 惨めなわたしのコト
findings.governingReading: Sakura says Rin ignored miserable me.
findings.explanation: The English moves from first-person wounded self-reference to a detached third-person girl.

findings.highlight: a blind plea
findings.evidenceJa: 出口のない懇願
findings.governingReading: Her hatred is an exitless plea directed toward the world and herself.
findings.explanation: Blind substitutes lack of sight or judgment for the absence of any escape.

findings.highlight: My eyes and hair were changed
findings.evidenceJa: 目も髪も姉さんとは変わっていって
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s eyes and hair progressively changed away from Rin’s.
findings.explanation: The English removes the sister comparison that ties bodily alteration to estrangement.

findings.highlight: They taught my body
findings.evidenceJa: 体に直接刻んで
findings.governingReading: The Makiri engraved their instruction directly into Sakura’s body.
findings.explanation: The English converts invasive inscription into education of the body.

findings.highlight: Once they put me with the worms
findings.evidenceJa: 蟲倉に放り込まれれば
findings.governingReading: When Sakura was thrown into the worm storehouse, even breathing required permission.
findings.explanation: The English weakens violent confinement and removes the established location.

findings.highlight: But Rin slashes away the shadows without a word.
findings.evidenceJa: 泣いて縋ってくる少女を、彼女は無言で斬り伏せる。
findings.governingReading: Rin silently cuts down the attacks of the crying girl who clings to and implores her.
findings.explanation: The English replaces Sakura herself as the emotional and grammatical object with impersonal shadows.

findings.highlight:
I’m crazy.
there’s something wrong with me.
findings.evidenceJa: どうかしてますよね。
findings.governingReading: Sakura says something is wrong with her, seeking agreement.
findings.explanation: The English prints two competing renderings and introduces the harsher insanity label.

findings.highlight:
the more delighted they became and
the more they tampered with my body.
findings.evidenceJa: あの人たちはわたしに手を加えていった。
findings.governingReading: The more Sakura begged, the more her abusers altered her body.
findings.explanation: The English invents increasing delight as a separate reaction.

findings.highlight:
Her
oppressed
wounded
soul.
findings.evidenceJa: 傷ついた魂。
findings.governingReading: The narration names a wounded soul.
findings.explanation: The English prints an unsupported oppressed alternative alongside the source-supported wounded.

findings.highlight: But.
findings.evidenceJa: それを。
findings.governingReading: The repeated object fragment “That…” carries Rin’s reception of Sakura’s plea forward.
findings.explanation: The English changes an unresolved object into an adversative conjunction.

findings.highlight: Not a single word of sympathy.
findings.evidenceJa: 一切同情しなかった。
findings.governingReading: Rin feels no sympathy whatsoever.
findings.explanation: The English frames the absence as unsaid words rather than absence of the feeling itself.

findings.highlight: being a monster doesn’t sound so bad.
findings.evidenceJa: 化け物になったのならそれはそれでいいんじゃない？
findings.governingReading: Rin coldly says that if Sakura became a monster, that state can simply stand as it is.
findings.explanation: Doesn’t sound so bad softens uncompromising acceptance into mild positive evaluation.

findings.highlight: I never thought it was painful.
findings.evidenceJa: 苦しいと思った事は一度もなかった。
findings.governingReading: Rin says she never once experienced herself as suffering.
findings.explanation: The English narrows broad hardship and distress to physical pain.

findings.highlight: what cruel treatment you’ve received.
findings.evidenceJa: どんなに酷い日々を送ってきたか
findings.governingReading: Rin says she does not know what terrible days Sakura has lived through.
findings.explanation: The English turns Sakura’s continuous lived days into discrete treatment received from others.

findings.highlight: She just tells her younger sister the truth.
findings.evidenceJa: 事実だけを口にして
findings.governingReading: Rin states facts and nothing more to her suffering sister.
findings.explanation: Truth removes the limiting only-facts stance and can endorse Rin’s judgment as a single truth.

findings.highlight: I never thought I was blessed.
findings.evidenceJa: 一度も思えた事はなかった
findings.governingReading: Rin says she was never once able to feel that she was blessed.
findings.explanation: The English removes incapacity and can read as a chosen belief.

findings.highlight: She stares back at Matou Sakura, with all emotion contained in her words.
findings.evidenceJa: 精一杯の気持ちを込めて、間桐桜という少女を見返した。
findings.governingReading: Rin looks directly back at Sakura with all the feeling she can muster placed into the gaze.
findings.explanation: The English assigns emotion to her words rather than her look.

findings.highlight: who wanted everything from her but received nothing
findings.evidenceJa: 持っていて欲しかったものを一欠片も持たないクセに
findings.governingReading: Rin possesses not one fragment of the quality Sakura had wanted her sister to possess.
findings.explanation: The English makes Sakura want and fail to receive everything from Rin, reversing possession and desire relations.

findings.highlight: says she’s still pure and clean!
findings.evidenceJa: 自分だけはキレイなままだと言い張って
findings.governingReading: Sakura accuses Rin of insisting that she alone remains clean.
findings.explanation: The English removes the exclusionary only-self contrast central to Sakura’s resentment.

findings.highlight: weakness against Matou Sakura.
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐桜に対する弱さ
findings.governingReading: Entrusting their problem to Shirou was Rin’s emotional weakness toward Sakura.
findings.explanation: Against frames tactical inferiority or antagonism instead of vulnerable attachment.

findings.highlight: finishes the battle.
findings.evidenceJa: あっさりと勝負を決めていた。
findings.governingReading: At that instant, Rin settles the contest with striking ease and simplicity.
findings.explanation: The English removes the effortless abruptness that recontextualizes her apparent strain.
